sections.title: E-commerce SEO
sections.text: Shoppers can reach your store by searching for a whole category, a specific product or a comparison between options. So we organize your store's pages around what customers search for at each stage, and we find what's stopping Google from reaching your key categories and products. Our goal is for visitors to land on a useful page that helps them choose and buy, and for you to see the impact in orders and revenue, not just traffic.

sections.title: From category to product
sections.text: Someone searching for “kids' bedroom furniture” hasn't made up their mind yet, while someone searching for a specific size or model is close to buying. We give the category page a clear role: presenting the options and helping shoppers narrow them down. Then we make sure the product page answers questions about size, specifications, availability and delivery using the information the store actually has. That way, each page serves a different question instead of the category and the product competing for the same search term.

sections.label: The categories and products that deserve priority
sections.title: Where is your store losing visibility?
sections.text: We review which categories deserve to rank, which products are available and the links that lead to them. Filters can create many near-identical pages or generate titles customers don't care about, so we don't apply one rule to every store. We choose what's useful to searchers and has content of its own, and we handle duplicate or unavailable pages based on your store's actual situation. We also check how fast pages load on mobile, because a customer may reach a product and leave before getting a proper look at it.

sections.title: What does SEO success mean for a store?
sections.text: Rankings and clicks help us understand reach, but they're not where improvement decisions end. We track the performance of category and product pages, plus orders and revenue from organic search, whenever the measurement tools are set up for it.

sections.label: Google Analytics

items.question: Should every filter page appear in search results?
items.answer: No. We only index a filter page when people actually search for it and it has content of its own that's useful to searchers. We keep the rest from creating duplicates, based on your store's data.

items.question: What happens to products that are out of stock?
items.answer: It depends on the product. If it's coming back, we keep its page and make availability clear. If it's discontinued for good, we send visitors to a suitable alternative or to its category.

items.question: Should we start with category pages or product pages?
items.answer: Usually with categories, because they attract broader searches and send visitors on to products. Then we move on to the products closest to an order. This may vary depending on your store's data.

items.question: How do we know SEO is affecting sales?
items.answer: When tracking is set up correctly, we connect organic visits to add-to-carts, orders and revenue, rather than looking at traffic alone.
